name: install_bioc
title: Install a development package from the Bioconductor git repository

origin.description: Clone a Bioconductor package repository and install it with R CMD INSTALL.
origin.usage: install_bioc(repo, mirror = getOption("BioC_git", "https://git.bioconductor.org/packages"), git = c("auto", "git2r", "external"), dependencies = NA, quiet = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: repo
arguments.text: Package name, or release/package such as 3.21/BiocVersion. release uses the configured Bioconductor release.

arguments.name: mirror
arguments.text: Git mirror. The default is the BioC_git option, otherwise https://git.bioconductor.org/packages.

arguments.name: git
arguments.text: auto uses an external git client when git2r is not installed.
Further arguments are passed to install.packages. lib is the library directory and is accepted.

origin.details: The branch is RELEASE_x_y from the release in the specification. The configured release is used when the specification does not name one.
origin.example: install_bioc("3.21/BiocVersion", dependencies = FALSE, upgrade = "never", quiet = TRUE, build = FALSE, lib = lib, git = "external")

translation.description: Clone a Bioconductor package repository and install it with R CMD INSTALL.
translation.usage: install_bioc(repo, mirror=None, git='auto', dependencies=NA, quiet=False, lib=None)

arguments.text: Further arguments are passed to install.packages. lib is the library directory and is accepted.

translation.details: The bundle is downloaded with urllib and installed with R CMD INSTALL into lib. A check uses a fresh temporary library and does not write to ~/R/library. The release branch is built from the specification. bioc_version supplies the configured release when the specification says release.
translation.example: install_bioc("3.21/BiocVersion", dependencies=False, upgrade="never", quiet=True, build=False, lib=lib, git="external")
